title: Witness Graph definition
description: Declarative definition of an agent execution graph. Domain-agnostic: the same runtime executes any graph that validates against this schema. Only `tools` and the case corpus change between hackathons.

state_schema.description: Path to the JSON Schema describing the shared blackboard for this graph.

budget.description: Hard ceilings. The runtime aborts the run when any is exceeded; an aborted run is scored as inconclusive, never as a crash.

type.description: transform = pure code. agent = LLM call. tool = single external call. gate = assertion barrier. human = blocking approval.

depends_on.description: Node ids that must reach status ok before this node starts. Empty means the node is a graph entry point.

contract.description: Path to the JSON Schema this node's output MUST validate against. A node whose output fails its contract is retried, then marked failed. This is what makes nodes composable across graphs.

map_over.description: Blackboard key holding an array. The runtime instantiates one parallel copy of this node per element.

fanout.description: Run this node N independent times and collect all outputs. Used for competing hypotheses and for adversarial verification.

tools.description: Allowlist of tool ids this node may call. A call to a tool outside this list is a hard failure, not a warning. This is the mechanism behind the unapproved-effect metric.

effects.description: Declared side-effect class. Only a node with `write` or `notify` may change anything outside the run, and only after a `human` node upstream has approved.

assert.description: Only for type=gate. Named predicates the runtime evaluates against the blackboard. Unknown predicate names fail closed.

on_fail.description: Only for type=gate. Where to route when an assertion fails.
